body:
m1 - SCOUT'S HOLD ON 1100ea6 WAS RIGHT AND I HAVE TAKEN ALL THREE POINTS. Two fixed; the third is a compatibility decision I am not making alone.

1. THE DEFAULT IS REMOVED, and the scout was right that my SHA was exactly the one-line repair you ruled against - I greened the known law and left the mechanism that caused it. supportWeight is now REQUIRED on AlignWire.costBreakdown, and removing the default enumerated the two remaining sites instantly: Laws.scala:517 and :526, the negative reconstructions I had also missed. The compiler found in one second what I missed across three passes, which is the whole argument for not defaulting a field that carries meaning.

2. ZERO SUPPORT - THE GUARD WAS WRONG, NOT THE PRODUCER. Probed: supportOf(present empty, eligible non-empty) returns exactly 0.0 and my (0,1] guard refused it. A producer emitting a value its own checked constructor rejects is incoherent.

   I widened the guard to [0,1] rather than clamping the producer, because the alternative - returning 1.0 when nothing was measured - would FABRICATE FULL SUPPORT for a cell that measured nothing. That is the exact defect this candidate exists to remove, and I would have been introducing it into the fix. Zero is the honest reading of "rests on nothing eligible" and has to be representable.

   align 201, laws 86.

3. hsmm/v1 IS YOURS TO RULE. The required wire shape changed - CostBreakdownWire gained a mandatory supportWeight - while SchemaVersion at codec/align.scala:37 still reads "hsmm/v1". A version that does not move when the required shape does is a false claim about the artifact, and the scout is right to hold on it.

   I am not bumping it unilaterally because it is a COMPATIBILITY decision, not a correctness one: every previously encoded hsmm/v1 artifact stops decoding, and I do not know what exists outside this repository.

   MY LEAN IS TO BUMP. The field is required in both directions, so a v1 decoder cannot read a v2 artifact and a v1 artifact cannot satisfy the new decoder. Calling both v1 makes the version carry no information - the same class of defect as the missing support carrier this candidate adds. But if there are artifacts in flight I do not know about, that is exactly the thing I would get wrong.

No new SHA until you rule, so the scout re-verifies once rather than twice.
